cn.t: Critics find "Kinky Boots" a feel-good crowd-pleaser with catchy Cyndi Lauper songs and Billy Porter's charismatic performance, though some fault its formulaic book and overly safe approach to its drag-queen premise.

sg.ra: Multiple guides converge on rows G-L (Tickpick) / D-L (Tickadoo) as the Al Hirschfeld's true center-orchestra sweet spot. This house has an unusually shallow rake for a Broadway musical theatre — Reddit regulars specifically warn 'Orchestra has little to no rake,' so mid-rows behind any head height become a real problem. Rows G-L sit far enough back to minimize Moulin Rouge's set-piece sightline issues (the elephant and catwalk platforms at house left/right) while staying ahead of the mezzanine overhang that drops at row K.

Front orchestra at Hirschfeld is unusual for a Broadway house: the Moulin Rouge runway/Can-Can extension pushes performers well forward and above your eyeline, so front rows require craning and miss the show's upper-balcony stage action. Tickpick flatly says 'not recommend to sit in the first three or four rows,' and Tickadoo notes 'elaborate staging may be partially obscured when the action shifts to the upper levels' — a show-specific warning that wouldn't apply at most houses.

House-left orchestra is the better of the two side orchestras at the Hirschfeld because Moulin Rouge's elephant set piece lives stage-right — obstruction is 'worse on the right,' per multiple regulars. You still lose some far-stage-left action (from the runway and side catwalk), but trade-off is that actors including Christian routinely enter from this aisle. Reviewers repeatedly single out the left side for close actor access ('Jordan Fisher was two feet away,' 'Aaron entered from there at a couple of points').

House-right orchestra has the biggest sightline trade-off at the Hirschfeld but also the biggest actor-proximity payoff for Moulin Rouge specifically. Christian and the Duke both make their debut entrances on this side, and Satine and Nini exit this way — plus the stagedoor lines up with the right-side exits. The cost: the elephant set piece sits stage-right and regulars warn 'on the far right side you'll basically be paying to look at stairs.' Worth it only if you want the actor-traffic side and stagedoor access.

Front-center mezzanine is the specific seat that Moulin Rouge regulars recommend OVER center orchestra — unusual advice for a Broadway musical. The reason is show-specific: the production's scenic design fills the full proscenium top-to-bottom (balconies, ceiling drapes, windmill, elephant), and orchestra viewers 'miss a lot of the theatre's ceiling AND the floor of the stage.' The Hirschfeld mezzanine also juts close to the stage, so A-C feel close rather than distant.

The Hirschfeld mezzanine has an unusual quirk — a walkway between rows F and G — so row G seats have nobody seated directly in front of them. Regulars pitch G as a cheaper alternative to front mezz with effectively the same sightline over rows F. A reviewer who asked about row J 105-107 was told 'that view should be great, you might miss a tiiiny bit of action on the very front of the catwalk but nothing important.'

Mezzanine left is the safer side mezzanine at the Hirschfeld because the elephant — the biggest sightline hazard during Moulin Rouge — lives stage-right. Reviewers from front-A mezz L report 'Jordan Fisher looked directly at my face when the show started' and 'awesome seat, very close to the stage,' but one specifically flagged that 'faces were blurry even though my vision is average' further back, so rear mezz left reads distances more than obstructions.

sg.n: Mezzanine Right (House Right) A-D (front mezz right)
sg.ra: Front mezzanine right is the single most-warned-against section in Moulin Rouge seating threads. The elephant set piece hangs at stage-right and sits directly in your sightline from this angle. 'Avoid mezz right ... unless you like staring at an elephant's trunk.' Multiple repeat viewers confirm the obstruction is specifically show-induced, not a permanent house flaw — worth the callout.

sg.n: Mezzanine Right (House Right) G-H (rear mezz right)
sg.ra: The rear section of Mezz R is the quirky bright spot of this wing: the rear mezz is staggered so that rows in the 'back half' physically stick out further than the row in front, eliminating head-in-front problems. First row of the rear ('eraic' calls it so) also has 'ample leg room here since it's in the first row of the rear which means there won't be anyone blocking a view.' Elephant obstruction flattens out as you move back and up.

Unique to Moulin Rouge at the Hirschfeld: the orchestra pit has been converted into two on-stage table sections flanking a performer catwalk — 5 tables (11 seats) house-left, 4 tables (8 seats) house-right. Performers interact directly with table guests throughout the show. Major caveats that don't apply to any other section: you must be seated 15+ minutes early or you forfeit the seat; no late seating at all in either act 'due to the scenic obstruction and safety'; bench seating at several tables is '2/3 the size of a regular chair' with little padding; children under 12 banned. You cannot see the full set from here and will be turning your head.
